headline: Meta may cap AI token spend per engineer in 1-2 years
summary: Meta's AI token spend could be capped per engineer within 1-2 years, according to Adam Mosseri.
details: Meta's Instagram head Adam Mosseri believes that AI token spend, the cost of processing AI prompts and responses, may need to be capped per engineer in 1-2 years. He likens it to managing other resources like payroll or operating expenditure.

Mosseri notes that the burn rate of a strong engineer might match their salary or employment cost. Meta shut down an internal AI token spend leaderboard after costs were on track to reach billions of dollars in 2026.
The company aims to manage token costs like any other resource. Mosseri expects token costs to decrease as AI model makers enter a pricing war, but for now, Meta has reduced unnecessary spending.
Mosseri's comments reflect a shift in how tech companies approach AI experimentation and cost management. Other companies, like Uber and Microsoft, have also reevaluated their AI spending.
caption:
Will Meta cap AI token spend per engineer soon?

Meta's Instagram head Adam Mosseri believes that AI token spend, the cost of processing AI prompts and responses, may need to be capped per engineer in 1-2 years. He likens it to managing other resources like payroll or operating expenditure.

Mosseri notes that the burn rate of a strong engineer might match their salary or employment cost. Meta shut down an internal AI token spend leaderboard after costs were on track to reach billions of dollars in 2026.

The company aims to manage token costs like any other resource. Mosseri expects token costs to decrease as AI model makers enter a pricing war, but for now, Meta has reduced unnecessary spending.

Mosseri's comments reflect a shift in how tech companies approach AI experimentation and cost management. Other companies, like Uber and Microsoft, have also reevaluated their AI spending.
